newsitem.title: UK: London gold fixes barely changed after US data.
newsitem.headline: London gold fixes barely changed after US data.

text.p: Gold and silver prices perked up but only briefly when stronger-than-forecast US economic data was taken to be a precursor of rising inflation on Wednesday.
First quarter GDP rose 5.6 percent, against expectations for a 4.1 percent rise and the implicit price deflator rose 2.3 percent versus expectations for a 1.7 percent rise.
A short covering rally in gold was turned round at $341.25 per ounce, the day's high before profit-taking took gold to an afternoon fix at $340.15, down $0.30 from them morning fixing.
Shortly after the fixing the Comex June contract was back to near unchanged at $341.70 having peaked at $343.20 during its first half hour of trading.
Precious metals prices had firmed on Tuesday as well, lifted by a bond rally and weaker dollar on the back of data on wage inflation that showed above forecast trends.
"U.S. data coming through with some unexpected inflationary signals are about the only thing gold's got going for it at the moment," one dealer in London said.
Bullion had been pushing to get back over $340.00 in earlier European dealings on Wednesday but dealers said the impetus was half hearted at best.
"There is good support at $340.00 but my gut feeling is that this is just a respite. It will go lower. You've still got that overhang of central bank selling," one dealer said.
Silver also made a brief move higher also based on short covering following the US GDP release but like the gold move, profittaking cut it off.
It got as far as $4.74 bid, up eight cents, before slipping back to $4.69/$4.71, still two cents above the opening level.

Silver's technical background was not constructive since a long term trend line broke last week signalling a possible test of support at $4.50 although interim support seemed to have been established at $4.65, dealers said.
Platinum and palladium held their recent ranges although both were about a dollar down on the Tuesday close at $371.50/$372.50 and $156.00/$157.00 respectively.

Some dealers said lending of one-year palladium had been more evident over the past couple of days than recently in the very tight market. "This could bring spot down eventually if it continues," a dealer said.
But no big down move was likely in either platinum or palladium prices until Russia is seen to begin 1997 supply talks with Japan, he added.
